title: Push to light

brief.story: The bench's call light should come on only while someone holds its button. The LED and its resistor are already wired; the loop has a gap where the button goes.
brief.goal: Make LED1 light at 10–25 mA only while the push button is held, and go dark when it's let go.

hints: There's a gap between column 3, where the + wire lands, and column 6, where R1 starts. The button goes across it.
Take the push button from the box and click a hole in column 3, then one in column 6.
A wire across the gap would light the LED for good. The button has to be the only way across.
debrief: A push button is a switch you hold. Held, it joins column 3 to column 6 and the loop is complete, so (9 V − 2 V) ÷ 330 Ω = 21.2 mA flows. Let go, and the loop is broken and nothing flows anywhere in it. In series, one gap stops the current everywhere, which is why a single switch can turn off a whole circuit.
